description:
Find and remove dead, stale and duplicated CODE, so the tree is what it claims to be.

RUN THIS LAST, DELIBERATELY. It carries a high number because a cleanup that runs before the work is finished deletes scaffolding that was about to be used, and then the next tasklist re-adds it. The roadmap should be substantially complete before this executes.

WHAT COUNTS AS DEAD. Unreferenced modules, functions and files; duplicated implementations of one behaviour; code behind flags that can no longer be set; scripts nothing runs; dependencies nothing imports; commented-out blocks kept 'just in case'. What does NOT count: code a test exercises, code an external consumer calls, and code that is deliberately unexercised and says so.

THE STANDARD OF PROOF, AND IT IS THE WHOLE TASKLIST. This portfolio has repeatedly found things that LOOKED dead and were not — a Prolog corpus reached by a path nobody found, `content_qa` declared callerless when it had a caller, `docs/studioos` cited by 93 files. Deletion is irreversible in effect even when git remembers, because nobody re-reads a deleted file. Every removal names the search that found nothing.

SCOPE NOTE: this repo is specification plus skeletons and **nothing moves bytes yet**. 'Dead code' here means scaffolding that no longer matches the spec it was written against, not unreachable runtime paths — there is barely a runtime. Be correspondingly careful: a skeleton is not dead because it is unused.

PAIRED WITH THE DOCS SWEEP, WHICH RUNS AFTER. Removing code changes what the docs should say, so the docs tasklist depends on this one. Do not fix docs here beyond what a removal strands.

userStories.title: An inventory, measured before anything is removed
userStories.notes: Verify green for everything that could run: .chief/verify.sh 3 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed — PASS Swift build, PASS Swift tests (46 passed: 4 upload-path, 39 state-machine vectors, 3 I6 transport vectors), PASS TypeScript typecheck, SKIPPED Gradle build (no JDK on PATH, so UNVERIFIED not passed). Also ran the four cheap CI gates directly: check-single-fixture.sh PASS ("one fixture at Tests/Conformance/vectors.json, referenced by both ports"), verify-skip-policy.sh "all assertions passed", check:control-surface "spec remains control-surface only", drift-control.sh --port swift "2 controls ran, 0 skipped, 0 failures". Docs-only change touching no Kotlin, so the Gradle skip strands nothing in this story. ARTIFACT: docs/reference/dead-code-inventory.md (289 lines), indexed in docs/README.md. NINE SEARCHES, each named with its command and scope (S1-S9): per-type and per-function reference counts over all 54 Swift types / 84 Kotlin types / every function in both ports; a 6-normalised-line duplicate-block hash per language; commented-out-code and TODO scans; per-dependency import counts; version-guard vs minSdk/platforms comparison; and a per-script grep against ci.yml and verify.sh. FINDINGS. Genuinely dead, 6: resume_data is a write-only table (storeResumeData called at DefaultUploadEngine.swift:298, loadResumeData has 0 call sites and 0 mentions in docs/Tests/packages/integration); UploadDao.inState:22 (1 grep hit, its own declaration, and no Swift counterpart); WireDialect.Rufh Kotlin:62-91 (the ONLY type in either port with refcount 0 — every construction site passes Tus10, and vectors.json has 0 occurrences of dialect/Upload-Draft/partial-upload); androidx.core:core-ktx (0 `^import androidx.core` hits vs 8 room / 5 work / 19 coroutines / 13 okhttp3); UploadNotifications.kt:31 SDK_INT >= O against minSdk 26, condition can never be false; three redundant @RequiresApi(O) in StorageGovernor.kt. Deliberately unexercised, 8, NOT to be deleted: the ten EnumConverters @TypeConverter methods all report 0 call sites and the module cannot compile without them (kapt emits the calls, and kapt runs nowhere on this machine); renewLease/pruneCompleted uncalled in BOTH ports symmetrically and carrying a stated retention policy plus half of invariant I8; Swift SourceResolver.stageIfRequired:62 has 0 callers while its Kotlin twin is called at DefaultUploadEngine.kt:217 — the caller is missing, not the callee, and that is port drift not dead code; the nativeResumeUnavailable chain across 5 files whose terminal operation is a set-remove on a set never inserted into and never read, kept because wire-protocol.md:57-63 specifies the behaviour it is the skeleton of; consumer-rules.pro; the RN control surface (external consumers); the tusd harness (docs state why it is not in CI). Duplicated implementations, 3, ranked by drift cost: the six-arm HTTP-status-to-ErrorClass table written out VERBATIM twice in Swift at BackgroundSessionManager.swift:212-223 and ControlPlaneClient.swift:124-132, read on two different code paths and covered by no vector — worst of the three; the two Swift transports sharing 9 overlapping 6-line windows (create/head/terminate delegations plus the whole PATCH construction); and the .offsetAdvanced prefix duplicated at UploadStateMachine.swift:86-92 and :156-169. Kotlin had ZERO duplicate blocks. Undecidable, 4 classes, left in place: cross-repo consumers, kapt codegen, framework dispatch (URLSession/ConnectivityManager/OkHttp/WorkManager callbacks all report 0 call sites and are all mandatory), and reflection — searched for Class.forName/NSClassFromString/dynamicMemberLookup and found none. Two negatives worth recording: 0 commented-out code blocks in any source language, 0 unused Swift imports, and exactly one TODO (StorageGovernor.kt:97) which names future work rather than hiding an abandoned path.
acceptanceCriteria: Produce a checked-in inventory of candidates with, for each, the SEARCH that found it unreferenced — the command and its scope. A candidate list without its method is unreviewable, and this is the artifact a human approves before deletion.
Separate genuinely-dead from deliberately-unexercised. The second class exists here on purpose (refusal paths, guards, unreached tiers that say so) and deleting it removes a stated contract.
Include duplicated implementations as first-class findings, not just unused ones — two implementations of one behaviour is the failure mode that costs most later, because they drift.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: Removal, with the tree still green and the reason recorded
acceptanceCriteria: Remove what US-1 established, in reviewable steps rather than one sweep. A single commit deleting hundreds of lines across unrelated subsystems cannot be reviewed and cannot be partially reverted.
The full gate passes after each step. A removal that needs a test deleted to stay green is a removal of something live — say so and stop rather than adjusting the test.
Anything NOT removed that looked dead is recorded with why it survived. That record is worth more than the deletions: it is what stops the next sweep re-litigating the same files.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.

userStories.title: What the sweep could not decide
acceptanceCriteria: Report candidates the sweep could not resolve — reachable only through dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, or a consumer outside this repo — and leave them in place. An honest 'undecidable' list is a legitimate result.
State the limits of the method: what a static search over this tree cannot see. Cross-repo consumers are the obvious one, and this portfolio has already been bitten by exactly that.
GATES: the repo's own verify green.
